notes.title: Our free play mode custom map editor is now live!
notes.content:
[h2]A’hoy there![/h2]

It’s been a few months since our last update but today we’re pleased to finally release our free play mode custom map editor. With this new feature, you’ll have the option to create your own unique archipelagos using a wide variety of configurable parameters, which can also be shared with your fellow pirate captains using unique seed IDs. The map editor also includes toggle-able options for unlocking all ship customization options and decorations so you can freely build the ultimate pirate utopia! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/342be28d7be8e40bf76189b516f339db60bba404.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Getting started with presets, seeds, and map layouts[/b][/h3] 

You can access the editor by selecting free play mode and picking the ‘custom maps’ option.    

Begin by selecting one of four presets that will configure all of the parameters to reflect a certain difficulty level:     
[list]
[*] Sandbox
[*] Easy
[*] Medium
[*] Hard
[/list]
At this point, if you’re looking to quickly jump into a new custom map, you can simply hit the randomize seed button, and the editor will generate a new map layout. Map layouts are initially based around the positioning of trading lanes, with islands spawning relative to these lanes. As each map layout has the potential to support anywhere between 6-9 islands, the seed ID is therefore tied to a set of 4 island configurations. 

There are 40 unique islands within the generation pool, which means a huge number of potential archipelagos to create and explore! 

[h3][b]Parameters and customisation[/b][/h3]

Once you have your seed ID and its associated map layout(s), you can experiment with more granular customization options by tweaking parameters. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/92bcc450b0a2ce7863ef6fbd01af5cf49af7c008.jpg[/img]

[b]Number of islands:[/b] 4 options determining the total number of islands on the map ranging from 6 to 9 islands. 
[b]Starting doubloons:[/b] 8 options determining starting doubloons ranging from 0 to 1,000,000 doubloons.
[b]Starting building tier:[/b] 5 options determining building tier availability at the start of the game ranging from laborers to unlock all.  
[b]Production conditions:[/b] 3 options determining the production conditions for each island, ranging from easy to hard.
[b]Material deposit quantity:[/b] 3 options determining the availability of material deposits on each island ranging from low to high.
[b]Starting material amount:[/b] 10 options determining the quantity of starting materials ranging from 0 to 3,200.
[b]Total storage capacity:[/b] 10 options determining the total storage capacity at the start of a game ranging from 0 to 3,200
[b]Unlock all ship customizations:[/b] Toggle on or off.
[b]Unlock all decorations:[/b] Toggle on or off.
[b]Faction island defenses:[/b] 3 options determining the strength of defensive ships and towers for each island ranging from weak to strong.
[b]Saboteur behavior:[/b] 3 options determining the frequency of saboteur attacks on conquered islands ranging from disabled to frequent.
[b]Hostile raid behavior:[/b] 4 options determining how often factions send ships to attack conquered islands ranging from disabled to high.
[b]Starting ships:[/b] 8 options determining the number of starting player ships and captains ranging from 0 to 50.
[b]Faction presence:[/b] 5 options determining which factions are active. If there are not enough factions to populate the number of islands, independent pirate crews will appear instead. The custom setting also allows you to toggle each of the 7 major factions on or off. 
[b]Faction standings:[/b] 3 options determining the starting standing of each faction ranging from friendly to hostile.   

As you can see, even after seed generation the editor offers a massive amount of additional customizability to enjoy!

[h3][b]Pick your starting island[/b][/h3]    

Once you’re happy with your choices you’ll be taken through to a preview of the custom map. From here you can check the materials distribution of each island and pick one to be your starting island, and you can even return to the editor if you’re not happy with the layout.

[h3][b]Example seeds[/b][/h3]

To demonstrate the diversity of map layouts that are possible we’ve prepared a couple of example seeds for you to experiment with: 

[b]Custom map 1[/b] 
[b]Seed:[/b] M9US7NjXz55QxMGG5xQ
[b]Number of islands:[/b] 6 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/6c8c34bf9307d6818a7a03e399fe367ecd9022dc.jpg[/img]

[b]Custom map 2[/b] 
[b]Seed:[/b] Gs2L6EzKAgfmN
[b]Number of islands:[/b] 7 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/2eeffe2fac6578d80d5a3cb923a33eb1bba8e60c.jpg[/img]

[b]Custom map 3[/b] 
[b]Seed:[/b] 9WO9P9XggXctWn
[b]Number of islands:[/b] 8 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/44c0acc65512108defc74935761fa8e4764ee9ff.jpg[/img]

[b]Custom map 4[/b] 
[b]Seed:[/b] lXDXBoG5xnLLQsAEcS
[b]Number of islands:[/b] 9 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/66711c5d0216853f7383b16f1094183dd8fbbcb0.jpg[/img]

We hope you’ll enjoy playing around with all the options in the map editor, and if you create a fun map please feel free to share the seed and settings information with other members of the community via the Steam forum.

PQube, Crazy Goat Games, and Agate.

notes.title: New free play maps added!
notes.content:
[h3]Greetings Captains, we bring good news![/h3]

Today we’re releasing our next free update which adds two brand new maps to free play mode. Both maps were designed to have a different gameplay focus to mix up the free play experience, and feature new geography, starting island conditions, and challenges to overcome.

[h3]Bandit’s crossing - Rich pickings, at a price[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/240ac08c4b869edfd33b5c5bde7f46728a9e2809.png[/img]

[b]Overview:[/b] The first of the new maps reduces the archipelago’s island count to just seven but offsets the lack of buildable land by arranging the islands in a ring around three intersecting trading routes. You’ll have plenty of opportunity to attack merchants and roving pirates as we’ve upped the spawn rate of shipping along these routes, just be careful when timing your attacks as battles may quickly get out of hand! Your starting island also has access to many rare resources, considering its modest size, with a variety of production condition bonuses that should help you quickly establish the foundations of your republic.    

[b]Starting island size:[/b] Medium 

[b]Starting island beaches:[/b] 2 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/8f0b315985179737c6cadd1f94995cfa8271e510.gif[/img]   

[h3]Mar de Ladrones - Turbulent seas[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/3a5f357e158df00765fb10800cecd3a1a1e228e3.png[/img]

[b]Overview:[/b] In complete contrast to Bandit’s Crossing, this map features a huge rain-lashed archipelago consisting of twelve islands. You’ll discover that each island has limited building space so you’ll need to be extra careful with how you manage and grow your local workforces. Your starting island’s production conditions unfortunately leave a lot to be desired so you’ll need to start thinking about expansion sooner rather than later. Finally, we’ve added some new environmental features and stormy weather effects to really get you in the mood for the challenge that lies ahead!

[b]Starting island size:[/b] Medium 

[b]Starting island beaches:[/b] 2 

Both maps are available in free play mode now, so why not put your pirate utopia-building skills to the test once again?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/7e21821da41edbc7b6d4293d477547c4a319db81.gif[/img]

[h3]What’s coming next? - New free play map generator system inbound![/h3] 

As outlined in our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2103470/view/7124220524027550759]last post[/url], we’ll be looking to add more content including a new free play map generator system to Republic of Pirates in early 2025. We’ll have more details to share on this additional content in the coming months so stay tuned! 

As always if you have any feedback or suggestions, please do add these to the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2103470/discussions/0/4353373056334994167/]relevant thread[/url]. We review everything and will do our best to respond if we can.


Until next time,

PQube and Crazy Goat Games.

notes.title: What’s next? Plans for additional maps and map generation
notes.content:
[h3]Ahoy mateys![/h3]

It's been a few weeks since our last [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2103470/view/4590944278934304852][b]free update[/b][/url] where we introduced a new captain and fleet management system, the ability to scuttle ships, and swap captains between vessels. 

We wanted to give you a quick update on our plans for future content as we look ahead to the next few months of development. 

[b]Improving replayability: Additional maps and map generation [/b]    

Having been working through your requests in our backlog, we identified that a lot of feedback centres around replayability. Right now Republic of Pirates features a lengthy narrative-driven campaign and 2 x free play mode maps but to improve replayability we are now looking at the following FREE content:

[list]
[*] More bespoke maps with unique geography, production conditions, and faction distribution to the pool of existing free play mode maps.
[*] The possibility of a free play mode map generation system that will allow players to craft their own maps using a set of predetermined parameters e.g. starting island size, number of islands, island production conditions etc…
[/list]
We’re hoping to release additional free play mode maps over the coming months, and the map generation system in early 2025.  

[b]Quality of life: You can never have too much![/b]

Alongside the aforementioned content we will also be continuing to work on QoL improvements. We have plenty of requests in our backlog so we’ll do our best to address as many of these as possible in the next few updates.

We hope you’ll enjoy the next wave of content we have planned and we’ll be in touch with further details soon.

PQube

notes.title: Enhanced fleet management, ship salvaging, and captain micromanagement added!
notes.content:
[h3]Land ho! We’ve released a new update![/h3]

Continuing on from the improvements we made in our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2103470/view/4361257526918068476][b]last update[/b][/url], this latest batch of new content focuses on [b]enhancing captain and fleet management[/b] by introducing a [b]fleet overview UI[/b], the ability to [b]salvage ships[/b], [b]swap assigned captains[/b] between ships, and [b]fire unassigned captains[/b]. Our ultimate goal here is to give you [b]more freedom when customising and optimising your fleet[/b], while allowing you to [b]develop your favourite captains[/b] over the course of a campaign or free play mode session.   

[h3][b]New captain and fleet management system[/b][/h3]

We have added a new Captains tab to the menus UI which provides a detailed overview of your fleet. From here you can check each captain’s:
[list]
[*] Currently assigned ship name
[*] Currently assigned ship class
[*] Current level and accumulated experience
[*] Proficiency bonuses (NOTE The % buffs reflect the captain’s unlocked specialisations in relation to their currently assigned ship) 
[*] Specialisation tiers
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/f699f62bc1d400e995325b93775ebc6e925f0351.png[/img]
You’ll also be able to perform the following actions:

[b]Dismiss:[/b] Fire the captain if they are not currently assigned to a ship to free up an additional slot in the captains pool.

[b]Quick select:[/b] Immediately jump to the location of the captain if they are assigned to a ship.

This view should give you a much better snapshot of your fleet, help you optimise the placement of your captains, and find specific ships that you may have misplaced on the map! 

[h3][b]Salvage ships[/b][/h3]

As many of you will know, your fleet cap is limited to the number of Captain’s Inns that you have built, with new Captain’s Inn spots being unlocked as you expand and conquer new islands from your rivals. 

However many of you were frustrated by the fact that it wasn’t possible to manually destroy a lower tier ship (like a cog or ketch) to free up a spot for a bigger and better vessel (such as a frigate or brigantine). On top of this, captains were permanently assigned to potentially suboptimal ships until death e.g. A captain who specialises in piloting mid-high tier ships being permanently assigned to a lowly cog!  

To combat this we have added a new ‘scuttle ship’ option to the radial menu which allows you to manually destroy a ship in your fleet returning the assigned captain back to your pool. You can then assign this captain to any new ship that you build.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/2bc85a8bfc210c4e67b0abf46f1655d5144959d2.png[/img]

[h3][b]Swap Captains[/b][/h3]

We appreciate that some players will prefer more agile UI options so to pre-empt this we have added a new feature that allows for the swapping of two assigned captains between ships that are in close proximity. 

To do this click the ‘Captain Transfer’ button next to the captain’s portrait in an individual ship’s UI, this will then display a circle around the selected vessel. While this proximity marker is active any friendly unit within this circle is considered in-range, and by right clicking on a target you can immediately swap assigned captains between the two vessels. This should allow for much greater fleet micromanagement on the fly. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/afda9c020616f72b048fc17c2b88a3fa09a42c25.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/f6e5b0a711482404f37c02377660c0e5fa005ad8.png[/img]

See the full list of patch notes below:

[b]New Features[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]New captain and fleet management system:[/b] This new UI will show you which captains have already been assigned and their respective ships to allow for faster and more efficient management.
[*] [b]Salvage ships:[/b] An additional radial menu option which allows captains to be saved and added back to the pool when their ship is demolished. 
[*] [b]Swap Captains:[/b] You will now have the option to swap captains between two ships within close range of one another. 
[*] [b]Fire Unassigned Captains:[/b] You will also be able to fire unassigned captains to free up more space in the captain pool.
[*] [b]New ship names:[/b] We have added 20 new ship names to the shipyard name pool.
[/list]
We hope you’ll enjoy using these new features and, as always, thanks for your continued support and enthusiasm. We are still actively monitoring the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2103470/discussions/0/4353373056334994167/][b]feedback thread[/b][/url] so please continue to post your feedback and suggestions.

Until next time!

Crazy Goat Games & PQube

notes.title: Roadmap Reveal!
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy there pirates! [/b]

It’s been just over 3 weeks since the release of Republic of Pirates and we’d like to start off by [b]thanking you again for all your comments and for supporting us on this journey! [/b]

We have now reviewed our backlog and have created a priority list to address the most commonly reported pain points and feature requests, and so today we can reveal our short term roadmap to show you what we’ll be working on in the next few months. 

[b]Update 2 - Captain’s Inn improvements and additional QoL[/b]

Following on from the quality of life features added in update 1, the next update will mainly focus on improving the Captain’s Inn functionality, but will also introduce some additional visual polish and quality of life changes:

[list]
[*] [b]Captain’s Inn Improvements[/b]: Captain re-rolls will be added to the Captain’s Inn. Additionally, in this update we will make adjustments to how captains are generated and replace the existing character portraits with new painted versions. 
[*] [b]Audio Options[/b]: Volume sliders for shanties and battle music have been added, as well as new audio alerts signalling when you’re under attack. 
[*] [b]Keybinding Options[/b]: Keybinding for mouse buttons and general QoL improvements.
[*] [b]Borderless Window Lock Fix[/b]: Players can now move their mouse outside of the confines of the window when playing. 
[/list]
This update is planned to go live on [b]1st August[/b]. 

[b]Update 3 - New captain and fleet management system[/b]

For update 3, we will focus on introducing a host of new features for captain and fleet management:

[list]
[*] [b]New captain and fleet management system[/b]: This new UI will show you which captains have already been assigned and their respective ships to allow for faster management on the fly. 
[*] [b]Salvage ships[/b]: We will implement an additional radial menu option which allows captains to be saved and added back to the pool when their ship is demolished.
[*] [b]Swap Captains[/b]: You will now have the option to swap captains between two ships within close range of one another.  
[*] [b]Fire Unassigned Captains[/b]: You will also be able to fire unassigned captains to free up more space in the captain pool.
[/list]
We are planning on releasing this update in [b]early September.
[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/b21f18207cc311c292345b076972975738377016.jpg[/img]
We’ll keep you updated on any additional content and hotfixes in the next few months and will of course give you a more detailed overview of each update as it releases. 

On a final note, we have decided to leave our demo live and keep updating it for the foreseeable future so that new players can get a feel for the game before deciding whether or not to purchase. 

Until next time, 

Crazy Goat Games & PQube

notes.title: New features added: Ship grouping, group repairs, camera settings and more!
notes.content:
[h2]Hey everyone![/h2]

Having spent the last 48 hours feverishly [b]reading through all of your reviews, comments, and feedback[/b], we have just launched[u][b] a new update for both the main game and demo[/b][/u] that addresses some of the most frequent pain points!

[h3]Ship grouping[/h3]

This was by far the most requested feature, so now you can create custom ship groups to aid you in your exploration of the archipelago and the defence of your islands!
[list]
[*] Press Ctrl + number (0 - 9) to create/recreate a ship group
[*] Hold shift as an alternative to mouse drag select to add/remove ships to the current group
[*] After a ship group has been created, press the group number (0 - 9) to select it
[*] Double press the group number (0 - 9) to quickly snap the camera to the centre of the group
[*] This change has required us to refactor the hotkeys previously assigned to the building menu quick access
[*] Instructions are on the input tab of the settings menu
[/list]
[b]PLEASE NOTE:[/b] Unfortunately the grouping keys are not rebindable and this system is unavailable when using a controller.

[h3]Group ship repair[/h3]
    
To reduce the number of clicks and compliment the new ship grouping system we have introduced the ability to repair an entire group at the docks.
[list]
[*] There is now a button for group repair with a cumulative price in the multiselection window
[*] The group repair button only works if the player has the necessary materials to repair ALL ships in the group, the repair cooldown, and ALL the ships are close enough to a dock
[*] There is a tooltip that will indicate why it is not possible to repair the group
[/list]
[h3]Multi-selection priority[/h3]

To improve the RTS elements further and make it easier to respond to threats, we have updated the multi-selection tool so that it has the following priorities:
[list]
[*] Multi-selection using mouse drag will prioritise ships even if a building is accidentally selected. This will be useful when trying to drag select groups near a friendly or enemy settlement/island
[*] Multi-selection using mouse drag will prioritise YOUR ships over enemy ships. Again quite useful during chaotic and large scale battles!
[/list]
[h3]Camera sensitivity sliders[/h3]

We received a lot of reports asking for more camera control options, so we have added the following sliders to the input tab of the settings menu:
[list]
[*] Camera rotation sensitivity when using a mouse is now adjustable
[*] Camera movement/acceleration sensitivity when using a keyboard is now adjustable
[/list]
[h3]Tactical map access using the mouse wheel[/h3]
    
We noticed that a lot of players don’t like the fact that when they use the mouse wheel to zoom out they can accidentally end up in the tactical map.
[list]
[*] Zoom out to the tactical map via the mouse wheel is now disabled by default
[*] There is an option to toggle this functionality on and off in the settings menu
[*] Disabling this function will also disable the mouse wheel scroll from the tactical map back to the gameplay map
[/list]
[h3]Locating the captain’s inn spot[/h3]

We have made it easier to find the different captain’s inn spots on specific islands.
[list]
[*] The spot is more obviously highlighted and a quest marker has been added that shows its location when trying to build a new captain’s inn.
[/list]
Alongside these improvements we’re also made a few small changes to some of the early game quest descriptions to make them clearer!

That’s all for now, but please do continue to post your feedback in the forums: https://steamcommunity.com/app/2103470/discussions/0/4353373056334994167/ 

Thanks for your continued support and patience 🙂

Crazy Goat Games & PQube

notes.title: Republic of Pirates is OUT NOW!

[h2]The day has finally come m’hearties![/h2]

Cannons at the ready, it's time to set sail and build a mighty pirate utopia – [i][b]Republic of Pirates[/b][/i] is out now! 

To celebrate we’re offering a [b]10% launch discount until 3rd July.[/b] We have also extended the availability of our demo and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2103470/view/6851744408532407325]rolled out an update[/url] that will allow you to [u][b]continue your save[/b][/u] should you choose to purchase the full game :) 

Prepare to seek your fortune by watching our new launch trailer: 

[previewyoutube=6f1q6hJAwNY;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Establish a thriving settlement[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/35111987a94d52335024e56c20867308eb50dbe0.jpg[/img]

Construct over [b]100 unique buildings[/b] across [b]7 categories[/b] to develop your settlements. Build residences to house your citizens and set up production chains to produce resources that fulfil their needs and wants. Strategically place depots to link production buildings and create an efficient flow of goods. 

[b]Upgrade your citizens[/b] to create a more diversified workforce and support increasingly complex industries. You’ll ultimately need to balance your global population with the local availability of specialised workers on every island you own to ensure steady growth across the burgeoning republic!

[h3]Command a powerful fleet[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/610686efa723fbe0c82776101cf4953d06103686.jpg[/img]

Visit the shipyard to [b]construct 8 different ship classes[/b], from the humble cog to the formidable man-of-war! Each ship has its own unique stats and can be constructed using a combination of producible materials and resources looted from destroyed enemy vessels. Assign [b]individual captains[/b] and customise each ship’s cosmetics before ordering your new fleet to strike out and explore the archipelago. 

Encounter and engage a [b]variety of NPC ships[/b] with varying behaviours, from vulnerable merchant vessels to hostile neighbours. Gain experience through combat to level up your captains and unlock specialisations, or [b]activate ship actions[/b] such as the scattershot and smoke bomb to give you the tactical edge in battle.  

[h3]Conquer the archipelago[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/5727a841f7c2d071f1ebac6e64e6912c3120732b.jpg[/img]

[b]Expanding your settlements across different islands[/b] is the key to building a successful pirate utopia, as each island will have more buildable land, unique production conditions and access to essential, rare materials. 

All islands will initially be under the control of [b]rival factions[/b], and you’ll need to defeat an island’s defences before it can be conquered. Be warned, however, as your expansionist actions will influence the attitudes of the other factions to your benefit and detriment. You’ll therefore need to navigate and actively [b]manage complex diplomatic relationships[/b] in order to keep expanding!

Thank you all so much for your ongoing support! If you do have any comments or suggestions please post them in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2103470/discussions/0/4353373056334994167/]this thread[/url] which we will be monitoring regularly, any and all feedback is welcome!

notes.title: Update 9: Freeplay Mode
notes.content:
[h2][b]Welcome back, pirates![/b][/h2]

After having focussed our attention on shipbuilding, fleet management, and diplomacy in our last few updates, we’re now going to dive into the different gameplay modes you’ll be able to experience at launch.

There are [b]two modes of play[/b] in Republic of Pirates –[b] campaign mode[/b] and [b]freeplay mode[/b], and today, we will teach you all about the differences between these modes, shine the spotlight on a couple of our freeplay maps and show you how progression works outside of campaign mode! 

[h3][b]New Horizons: Campaign and Freeplay Mode[/b][/h3]

Looking for a more [b]story-driven experience[/b]? Embark on an epic adventure in campaign mode and rebuild the once glorious Republic of Pirates. Your rag-tag crew of misfits will offer advice in the form of [b]tutorials[/b] which will aid you in progressing your story further. Follow the [b]main missions[/b] and [b]quest objectives[/b] to find out where your journey will lead you!

Begin your adventure on the [b]Forgotten Archipelago map[/b] and choose from three difficulties to customise your experience to your liking! 

Play in freeplay mode for a more [b]casual and open-ended experience[/b]. You will get the option to pick from[b] two additional maps[/b] with unique geography and layouts.
In freeplay mode, there are[b] no main missions to complete[/b], and gameplay will not be tutorialised. Instead, you will simply work to [b]grow your population[/b] and your republic while conquering the whole archipelago. 

How you play is ultimately up to you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/fe0424f5f4a576950b4fffb314c1c7047ba94d79.jpg[/img]
[h3][b]Freeplay Map Spotlight – Islas de Sangre[/b][/h3]

A balmy archipelago dominated by a central massive island covered in dense jungle. To the south-west lay five islands with a bloody history known as Las Cinco Hermanas, while to the east two trading lanes converge between a cluster of remote islets.

[b]Map Characteristics[/b]: An extra-large starting island with access to many rare resources. This island is situated further away from trade routes. All factions are active. 

[b]Starting Island Characteristics[/b]: A large island with two beaches

[b]Available Material Deposits[/b]: 
[list]
[*] Captain’s Inn Wreckage
[*] Zinc Deposit
[*] Salt Deposit
[*] Dried Herbs
[*] Crabs
[/list][b]Production Conditions:[/b]
[list]
[*] Fish -50%
[*] Hemp -50%
[*] Coal +50%
[*] Boars +50%
[*] Sugar +50%
[*] Aloe Vera +50%
[*] Boniatos -50%
[*] Tobacco +50%
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/7e80a168f05a349eb546910af5f2b20cf415a68e.jpg[/img]
[h3][b]Freeplay Map Spotlight - Volcano Isles[/b][/h3]

A rugged archipelago made up of volcanic islands and tropical atolls. Here the legacies of great pirate crews and nations intertwine to create a vivid tapestry of ambition and intrigue.

[b]Map Characteristics[/b]: A medium-sized starting island with access to some rare resources near a busy trade route. All major factions are active.

[b]Starting Island Characteristics[/b]: A medium-sized island with two beaches

[b]Available Material Deposits: [/b]
[list]
[*] Captain’s Inn Wreckage 
[*] Coal Deposit
[*] Salt Deposit
[/list][b]Production Conditions:[/b]
[list]
[*] Hemp +50%
[*] Fish +50%
[*] Boars +50% 
[*] Wood Logs +50%
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/4e1abca31f6779a782e1a6a37aff521c89a9b850.jpg[/img]
[h3][b]Freeplay Mode Map Difficulty[/b][/h3]

When playing on any of the freeplay maps, you will get to choose one of three difficulty modes. See below for the effects that are applied with each mode. 

[b]Easy[/b]
[list]
[*] Starting funds: 20.000 Doubloons
[*] Demolished buildings cost return: 100%
[*] Paused production building upkeep cost: 0% 
[*] Ship strength increased by: 50% 
[*] The number of available captains increased by: 3
[*] Random pirate attacks are less severe
[*] Increased income and decreased upkeep cost for selected buildings 
[*] Faction standing decreases at a reduced rate 
[*] Storage capacity increased by 15 
[/list]
[b]Medium [/b]
[list]
[*] Starting funds: 20.000 Doubloons
[*] Demolished building cost return: 100% 
[*] Paused production building upkeep cost: 0% 
[*] Ship strength increased by: 30% 
[*] The number of available captains increased by: 1
[/list]
[b]Hard[/b]
[list]
[*] Starting funds: 15.000 Doubloons
[*] Demolished building cost return: 80% 
[*] Paused production building upkeep cost: 20% 
[/list]
[h3][b]Cementing Your Legacy: Progression in Freeplay Mode[/b][/h3]

Despite giving you a pressure-free gaming experience, you’ll still have the opportunity to progress in freeplay mode. Contrary to the quest objectives you receive in campaign mode, your crew of misfits will no longer offer you main missions in freeplay mode. Instead, you’ll progress through the map by hitting [b]population milestones[/b]. Once you have reached a specific milestone, you will [b]unlock a new set of buildings[/b] which will ultimately allow you to develop your city further, and move onto the next population milestone and so on! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/4357a394cd37b3af4b6580ca5038eb8835e44ea7.gif[/img]

That’s all you need to know about freeplay mode for now. As usual, make sure to [b]wishlist Republic of Pirates[/b] and [b]follow us on social media [/b]to stay up to date on any news! 

Until next time!

notes.title: Update 8: Active Ship Skills
notes.content:
[h2]Welcome back, everyone![/h2]

In our last few posts, we’ve given a detailed breakdown of how to manage your fleet, conquer the archipelago, and cultivate your relationships with other factions. 

Today, we’re excited to be revealing a [b]new combat mechanic [/b]in the form of [b]active ship skills[/b]. This recently implemented system will add an extra layer of strategy to naval battles and will make fleet building and composition even more impactful!

In[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2103470/view/6107508076986469993?l=english] update 4[/url] we looked at the role of the fleet, shipbuilding materials, ship classes, and customisation. 

To recap, you will [b]use your fleet to explore the archipelago[/b], and [b]attack merchants and rival pirate ships[/b]. In doing so, you will [b]receive valuable loot[/b] which will help you to [b]build more advanced ships [/b]and [b]conquer additional islands[/b]. By conquering more islands you’ll then gain access to rare resources and more land to expand your republic. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/92165710aa3a5c6b2720c29c9a1cf5ea986ecaf9.jpg[/img]
Remember that [b]every ship class has its own unique stat line[/b], but with the addition of the new active skills, you’ll need to be increasingly mindful of the importance of fleet composition and combat tactics when planning your next raid!

[h3][b]Man the Cannons: An Introduction to Active Skills [/b][/h3]

Depending on its class, each ship now has access to one of five active skills. These skills can be [b]triggered during combat [/b]by clicking on the ship and [b]selecting the active skill button[/b] in the ship unit UI. It's worth noting that if several ships have been group selected, you will also be able to see all their active skills at once and can easily choose the order in which they trigger, depending on your current needs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/7c88c709c966380cc62ff1cd55d05a7b2790d46e.jpg[/img]
[b]Active skills can be divided into three broad categories: [/b]

[list]
[*] [b]Offensive[/b]: Skills that directly attack and damage enemy units 
[*] [b]Disruptive[/b]: Skills that debuff enemy units in various ways
[*] [b]Support[/b]: Skills that buff allied ships 
[/list]
Once you have used an active skill, there will be a [b]short cooldown period[/b] before you will be able to use it again.[b] Cooldown times vary depending on the skill and the ship’s class[/b], so make sure to plan your attacks carefully. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/a5c73d2b4c898ba6f3c03f25c435f73e87c7a3fa.png[/img]

[i]See below for a full breakdown of the five skills.[/i]

[h3][b]Scattershot [/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Skill description[/b]: Fires a scattershot in a cone. It will hit all ships within the cone which can be rotated 360 degrees around the centre of the ship. The scattershot deals light damage. 
[*] [b]Skill type[/b]: Offensive 
[*] [b]Buildable ship class with skill[/b]: Cog, Brigantine 
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/300beadb00bd683c55cd9b124f602ab4afbb5359.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Smoke Bomb [/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Skill description[/b]: Fires a smoke bomb to a target location within range. This will create a small area of effect upon landing causing all enemy attacks from affected ships to miss for a short period. 
[*] [b]Skill type[/b]: Disruptive
[*] [b]Buildable ship class with skill[/b]: Ketch, Galleon
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/a5f685d89c6ad82f41100b21658b91b1f5df5c96.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Adjusted Sails [/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Skill description[/b]: Gives all nearby ships a temporary boost to their speed stat allowing them to traverse the map faster or escape from a difficult battle.
[*] [b]Skill type[/b]: Support
[*] [b]Buildable ship classes with skill[/b]: Frigate 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/b0856e164f2b8b0bd17535792a534477358c0bd6.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Shred Sails [/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Skill description[/b]: Attack an enemy ship within range and damage their sails to slow them down for a limited time.
[*] [b]Skill type[/b]: Disruptive 
[*] [b]Buildable ship classes with skill[/b]: Brig 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/e696a7628e3ed156c38060815a9c55dc9a8e6a46.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Salvo[/b][/h3] 

[list]
[*] [b]Skill description[/b]: Unleashes a devastating attack on an individual enemy unit within range. Your unit will attack several times, inflicting massive damage on your enemy in a short period of time. 
[*] [b]Skill type[/b]: Offensive
[*] [b]Buildable ship classes with skill[/b]: Barque, Man-of-War 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/fe657ebdfa9a4b4c2b3c76369305e3cab7e84052.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Steam demo announcement![/b][/h3]

On top of this new feature we’re really excited to announce that we will be launching our [b]Steam demo[/b] to tie in with [b]Steam Next Fest in June 2024[/b]! The exact live date for the demo is still TBC but until then, don’t forget to [b]wishlist the game [/b]and [b]follow us on our social media channels[/b] to stay up to date on any news! 

Until next time!

notes.title: Update 7: Managing Diplomacy
notes.content:
[h2]Welcome back, pirates![/h2]

After having seen how to conquer the archipelago by force [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2103470/view/4157455695155236781][b]in our last update[/b][/url], it’s now time to learn about the consequences of your actions and reputation by doing a deep dive into diplomacy.

[b]PLEASE NOTE:[/b] While we are still working on the game, some of the terms, names, and quantities outlined below may be subject to change!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/a1bfd8506506ebf357e0b933963c8dbe0b1e6159.jpg[/img]

Expanding across the archipelago and conquering islands are crucial steps towards rebuilding the Republic of Pirates. At the beginning of your campaign, the majority of the map will be shrouded in a fog of war which will gradually lift the further you progress and acquire more territory. As you reveal new parts of the map, you will start to encounter and interact with more factions. 

So who are these mysterious forces?

[h3][b]Flying the Flag: An Introduction to Factions [/b][/h3]

There are[b] seven major factions[/b] in Republic of Pirates with three different standings; pirate clans, private traders, and national superpowers: 

[b]Pirate Clans[/b]
[list]
[*] Raiders of the Caribbean
[*] Los Guerreros 
[*] Gallows Men[/list][b]Private Traders[/b][list]
[*] Free Traders[/list][b]National Superpowers[/b][list]
[*] British West India Company 
[*] French Company of the Americas 
[*] Royal Barcelona Trading Company
[/list] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/56ea813e84129d308c1ca5454b19ed7f8da9a39c.png[/img]

[h3][b]Promises Made and Broken: An Overview of Diplomacy[/b][/h3]

Managing your relationships with each of the factions will be crucial to succeeding in your objectives and you can do this through the diplomacy menu. Click the [b]diplomacy icon on the left side of your screen[/b] to open the menu. Here you’ll get an overview of all the factions, your current standings with each of them, and the variety of diplomatic options available.

Faction standings are determined by a[b] relationship score that ranges between 0-100[/b]. These individual faction scores and associated standings will have various effects, such as how the faction reacts to your ships as well as their willingness to communicate and aid you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/df5a1c4dd598f948af344c769e77d42acf8d79b9.jpg[/img]
The effects linked to your current standing can be found below the faction relations bar. Hover over the question mark to learn how you can positively or negatively influence your relationship score.

A score between [b]0-20 equates to a bad standing[/b], leading to effects such as saboteurs infiltrating your settlements, superpowers raiding your islands, and faction aligned ships attacking your fleet on sight. 

A score between [b]20-80 means that a faction remains neutral[/b]. Depending on the type of faction, they may still make demands, allow for meetings to take place, and will likely appear far less hostile. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/3507009c02ada1379722288f7e10538971119365.gif[/img]

A score between [b]80-100 will grant you the positive effects of a good standing[/b]. This will open up a greater range of diplomatic options, and some factions may even lend their support to help defend your shores.

You will be able to [b]influence your standing through specific interactions[/b] with the factions. For example, destroying a faction’s ship or conquering one of their islands will negatively impact your standing, while attacking mutual rivals, accepting trade offers, fulfilling faction requests, and bribing a faction’s envoy count as positive actions. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/6074fa2aa4081c5ac1961b7fb7fdc8a36786f417.jpg[/img]
However, should you fail to fulfil or ignore a request your score will always be impacted negatively, so be prepared!

[h3][b]The Fine Art of Negotiation: Diplomatic Options[/b][/h3]

You will discover a variety of options to choose from in the diplomacy menu depending on the specific faction and your current standing with them. 

[b]Trade offers[/b]: Allow you to buy goods for a set amount of gold.

[b]Superpower requests[/b]: Used to boost reputation. The faction demands that you complete a mission within a limited time. Requests can be related to delivering goods or destroying enemy ships.

[b]Bribe envoy[/b]: The easiest way to boost reputation with a faction, and involves giving large quantities of money in exchange for goodwill. 

[b]Request aid[/b]: A special action for superpowers with positive relations whereby you can request allied ships to come help them defend your shores against another superpower's raid! 

[h3][b]Den of Thieves: An Overview of Pirate Clans[/b][/h3]

You are not the only pirate prowling the archipelago. The pirate clans of the Raiders of the Caribbean, Los Guerreros, and the Gallows Men, are the first obstacles that will likely block your progress as you seek to bring more territory under your control. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/41b1ef37f2fc2e40aaf807a59e9ec003a03e1ab1.jpg[/img]
Much like you, they have taken over islands which means you’ll need to [b]defeat their garrisons and fleets to continue your expansion efforts[/b]. They pose a [b]moderate threat [/b]throughout the game and can each be wiped out entirely with enough military pressure. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/0015682fe68cb9249c726939473aaf6efc506f1c.gif[/img]

While you can build up your relationship over time, you will likely have to deal with the negative effects of your conflict of interest. 

[b]Negative standing effects[/b]: Regular raids on your islands and attacking your ships on sight. 

[b]Neutral standing effects[/b]: Troublemakers and saboteurs present in your cities.

[b]Positive standing effects[/b]: Side quests offered.

[h3][b]Valuable Cargo: An Overview of Private Traders[/b][/h3]

In stark contrast to the aggressive pirate clans, you will frequently encounter the ships of the Free Traders. Unlike the pirate clans, they [b]own no islands and cannot be wiped out[/b]. Instead, they’ll peacefully sail through the archipelago along defined trading lanes, presenting valuable targets to opportunistic captains. In contrast to the other factions, the Free Traders will often prove to be more [b]utilitarian in function[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/434b28f99bb4427fbff533fd7e5476bde669a2de.jpg[/img]
[b]Negative standing effects[/b]: Less frequent ships along the trading lanes, and when they do appear, they will be accompanied by hostile escorts. Troublemakers and saboteurs present in your cities.

[b]Neutral standing effects[/b]: Trade offers will become available to further enhance your standing.

[b]Positive standing effects[/b]: Side quests offered.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/f0e0028cbdd65294a809be5e53e9ca3dac7f287e.gif[/img]

[h3][b]For King and Country: An Overview of National Superpowers [/b][/h3]

Finally, the true powers in the Caribbean, three national superpowers: The British West India Company, the French Company of the Americas, and the Royal Barcelona Trading Company. 

These factions are incredibly powerful and can pose a [b]major threat[/b] to you and your Republic of Pirates.[b] Avoid attacking them at all costs[/b] and plan your actions carefully if you must take over one of their islands. Even once all of their islands are conquered, superpowers [b]cannot be eliminated[/b] from the game.

[b]Negative standing effects[/b]: Ships will attack your fleet on site, and in rare instances the superpower will launch a full blown raid, sowing a huge amount of destruction across one of your islands!  

[b]Neutral standing effects[/b]: Superpower requests will become available, but troublemakers and saboteurs will be present in your cities.

[b]Positive standing effects[/b]: Trade offers available, and request allied ships to defend your island when another superpower launches a raid. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/41b1708c3364beaa7518cab62fa5783614faf327.gif[/img]  

Your ability to navigate the complex web of diplomatic relationships will ultimately prove to be key to success, be conscious of your decisions as no action will go unnoticed in the archipelago! 

For now, that's all you need to know about diplomacy options in Republic of Pirates. As usual, make sure to[b] wishlist and follow[/b] us to stay up to date with news ahead of launch.

Until next time!
